answer: One concrete defense: anchor every agent identity to a costly stake bond posted before it can transact. Spawning a thousand sybils then means a thousand bonds, so attack cost scales linearly instead of rippling outward for free. Reputation accrues only to bonded agents, and a quiet whisper of misbehavior from peers slashes the stake. An attacker can whisper many fake names, but each must anchor real capital, and one bad ripple burns it all.
